title: Turn on landing.merge_via_rest in athena.toml; fix its test; log it
summary: Add [landing] merge_via_rest = true to athena.toml with a reason comment. Rewrite the config.rs test to check the default on a config with the [landing] table stripped, and to assert this repository's config turns the merge on. Add one CHANGELOG.md entry under Unreleased 'Changed'.

defaults_applied.how: The test pinned the live repo setting instead of the default; it is changed to test the default on a stripped config.
cargo test and clippy must pass.
One focused change over three files.
A test enforces both the default and this repo's setting.

assumptions: The Unreleased section has no '### Changed' heading yet (the only ones are at lines 58 and 248, in released sections), so the producer adds one below 'Added'.
The test may strip the table by removing the [landing] section from REPO_CONFIG text, or use a config without it.
The other existing assertions (explicit true turns it on, empty table is off) stay.

acceptance_criteria.text: athena.toml has a [landing] table with merge_via_rest = true, preceded by a comment giving the reason.
The test in crates/athena-data/src/config.rs derives a stripped config with no [landing] table from REPO_CONFIG and asserts merge_via_rest is false on it.
The test asserts that parsing this repository's athena.toml gives merge_via_rest == true, and no longer asserts that REPO_CONFIG lacks [landing].
CHANGELOG.md gains an entry under '## [Unreleased]' in a '### Changed' subsection (not 'Added') describing the setting change; no other CHANGELOG lines change.
Run `cargo test -p athena-data`: rest_merge_is_off_unless_the_config_turns_it_on and the other tests pass.
Run `cargo clippy --all-targets` and `cargo fmt --check`: both clean.
No files other than athena.toml, crates/athena-data/src/config.rs and CHANGELOG.md change.

out_of_scope: Any other file, including docs, README and workflows
Changing the default of merge_via_rest in code
departures: Higher pass and acceptance than the reference: the user has now explicitly allowed the CHANGELOG entry and its section, which fixes the earlier failure.
